title: Add config migration for route groups + tier defaults (non-breaking)
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Introduces a backwards-compatible config migration that adds RouteGroup + TierDefault concepts while preserving existing per-route/per-tenant limit behavior; required for tier-aware enforcement rollout.
body:
Summary
This PR adds a non-breaking config migration that introduces (1) Route Groups and (2) Tier Defaults in the control-plane config model, while preserving existing customer configs and enforcement behavior.

Context
Hot-route capacity protection requires us to reason about limits/budgets by logical route group (e.g. chat, embeddings, rerank) and apply tier-aware defaults (enterprise vs best-effort) without forcing customers to re-author configs or causing accidental limit changes.

Key changes
- Adds new config schema objects:
  - route_groups: named groups with route matchers (exact + prefix; no regex).
  - tier_defaults: default policy blocks keyed by tier + route_group.
- Adds a migration runner that:
  - Detects legacy configs that only define per-route or global quotas/limits.
  - Materializes equivalent route_groups for known core routes and assigns routes to groups.
  - Backfills tier_defaults with values derived from legacy limits.
  - Writes the migrated config under a new versioned namespace, leaving original legacy fields intact.
- Adds an evaluation compatibility layer:
  - If tier_defaults are present, they are used as the base.
  - Legacy per-route/per-tenant overrides continue to apply last-write-wins.
  - If tier_defaults/route_groups are absent, behavior is unchanged.
- Adds guardrails:
  - Migration is idempotent.
  - Migration is opt-in via feature flag: hot_route_config_v2_migration.
  - Dry-run mode logs diff summary without persisting.

Non-goals
- No customer-visible UI changes.
- No changes to billing or metering behavior (only config shape).
- No rewrite of fairness scheduling; this only sets up config primitives.

Why this is safe
- We preserve legacy fields and only start reading the new fields when the flag is enabled.
- Tier defaults are derived from the existing config (no new rate limit values introduced by default).
- Overrides apply after defaults; customers with explicit per-route/per-tenant config should see no changes.
- Adds validation to prevent accidental widening/narrowing:
  - For each migrated route, computed effective limits for tier=enterprise/best-effort must match legacy effective limits (within rounding for window boundaries).

Migration details
- Known route groups in this PR:
  - chat_completions: /v1/chat/completions
  - completions: /v1/completions
  - embeddings: /v1/embeddings
  - rerank: /v1/rerank
  - misc: catch-all (only used when legacy config was global-only)
- Matching order: exact > prefix > misc.
- Tier mapping:
  - enterprise: accounts with tier in {enterprise, dedicated_enterprise}.
  - best_effort: self_serve + trial + untagged.

Observability
- Adds structured log line on migration apply:
  - config_migration=route_groups_tier_defaults
  - tenant_id (hashed)
  - before_version / after_version
  - changed_route_count
  - validation_result
- Adds a metric for migration outcomes:
  - control_plane.config_migration.applied_total{result=success|skipped|failed, reason=...}

Testing
- Unit tests for:
  - Legacy-only config -> v2 config equivalence
  - Idempotence (apply twice yields identical v2 output)
  - Override precedence (tier_defaults + legacy overrides)
  - Matcher precedence (exact > prefix)
- Integration test (config service + policy engine contract) behind the flag:
  - Loads a representative enterprise tenant config and verifies effective limits match pre-migration.

Rollout plan
1) Land this PR with flag default OFF.
2) Enable dry-run in us-east canary control-plane to generate diffs and validate no unexpected widening.
3) Allowlist a small set of enterprise accounts; enable apply.
4) Expand allowlist, then region-by-region.
Rollback
- Disable flag; system reverts to legacy evaluation paths.
- v2 configs remain stored but are ignored.

Files/areas changed (high level)
- control-plane/config-schema: add route_groups + tier_defaults
- control-plane/migrations: add migration runner + dry-run
- control-plane/config-eval: compatibility layer and precedence logic
- policy-engine/contracts: update config contract version header
- tests: migration equivalence + idempotence

Commits (squash summary)
- control-plane: introduce RouteGroup + TierDefault schema (versioned)
- migrations: add v2 backfill + idempotence + dry-run diff
- eval: apply tier defaults first, then legacy overrides
- validation: compare effective limits pre/post migration
- tests: migration fixtures + contract integration test

Review notes / discussion
- Ethan Park: asked for explicit precedence rules + examples. Added a 'Resolution order' section to schema docs + tests that lock precedence.
- Jordan Lee: requested deterministic output ordering to avoid noisy diffs. Added stable sorting for route_groups and tier_defaults blocks.
- Amara Diallo: flagged risk of route matcher drift between gateway and control-plane. Added shared route canonicalization helper and exported constants.
- Cole Summers: requested proof that quotas (windowed) don’t shift due to rounding. Added window alignment logic + asserts in test fixtures.
- Kaitlyn Nguyen: requested that migration logs avoid raw tenant IDs. Added hashing + sampling.

Checklist
- [x] Flagged + safe defaults
- [x] Idempotent migration
- [x] Equivalence validation for effective limits
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Dry-run support for rollout

CI
- build: pass
- unit tests: pass
- integration tests: pass
- lint/format: pass

Merge
Merged via squash to main on 2026-01-13.

Follow-ups
- Wire dry-run summaries into internal dashboard panel (ENG-4928)
- Expand route_groups with additional endpoints as we graduate more routes into protection (PM-882)
- Add Console internal view of v2 config objects once backend hooks are in (PR later in console backend series)
closing_notes: Enables non-breaking adoption of route groups + tier defaults required for tier-aware enforcement; rollout remains gated by hot_route_config_v2_migration flag.
